description: Conversational learning cards with subtitle, body paragraphs, and takeaway per card.

cards.title: Good Ideas Need Distribution
cards.subtitle: A strong idea can die quietly if it never reaches the right people.
body: Creators often over-focus on crafting and under-focus on how the work travels.
Packaging, channels, and timing are part of idea quality in practice.
cards.takeaway: An idea is only useful when it can move.

cards.title: Constraint Improves Creativity
cards.subtitle: Unlimited options often produce weaker decisions, not better ones.
body: Deadlines, limits, and format boundaries force sharper tradeoffs and clearer thinking.
Many standout works come from solving inside constraints rather than escaping them.
cards.takeaway: Constraints turn vague ambition into concrete output.

cards.title: Originality Is Usually Recombination
cards.subtitle: Most fresh ideas are old pieces combined in a new frame.
body: Cross-domain reading helps because it increases the pieces you can connect.
Novelty often comes from synthesis, not isolated genius.
cards.takeaway: Collect diverse inputs to create uncommon combinations.

cards.title: Timing Matters as Much as Insight
cards.subtitle: Being right too early can look identical to being wrong.
body: Markets, tools, and audience readiness change whether an idea can stick.
Sometimes the insight is sound, but the environment is not ready yet.
cards.takeaway: Fit the idea to the moment.

cards.title: Feedback Should Shape, Not Dilute
cards.subtitle: Input helps when it sharpens intent, not when it blurs it.
body: If you accept every suggestion, the work loses coherence and voice.
Use feedback to test clarity and usefulness, then decide deliberately.

cards.title: Small Experiments Beat Big Theories
cards.subtitle: Testing quickly often teaches more than debating endlessly.
body: A rough prototype with real users reveals what assumptions survive contact with reality.
Iteration lowers risk and improves judgment over time.
cards.takeaway: Learn with evidence, not only argument.

cards.title: Taste Develops Through Repetition
cards.subtitle: Creative judgment grows from making many attempts, not waiting for one perfect one.
body: Early work is usually uneven. Volume with reflection closes the gap between taste and execution.
Consistency builds intuition about what works and why.

cards.title: Simplicity Is a High-Skill Choice
cards.subtitle: Clear ideas often require more effort than complicated ones.
body: It takes real understanding to remove noise without losing meaning.
People remember what they can explain, not what sounds impressive.
cards.takeaway: Make it simple enough to carry.
